mappings.note: B inversely proportional to r for a straight current-carrying wire; the reason clause is LO-4's distance law.
The magnetic force does no work on a moving charge, so its energy is unchanged - LO-1.
Three-pin connection and the earthed metal body of an appliance; LO-7 names earthing.

The turns of a solenoid attract because parallel currents attract - a force on a current sitting in another current's field (LO-1), with LO-4 supplying that field. Not LO-4 alone: the assertion is about a force.
Whether random electron motion gives a net force on a conductor - the condition for the LO-1 force to exist at all.
Torque on a current-carrying coil in a field and its equilibrium orientation - the motor principle, LO-1.
Asks for Oersted's observation, that every current-carrying conductor has a field around it. That is LO-4's premise; the scientist's name is incidental here.

Name-only recall (William Gilbert, earth's magnetic field). No outcome in this frame covers earth's magnetism or the history of its discovery, so goal level under 'explores the nature of Science'. Frame gap, not a stretched code.
Field strength near a wire versus the current in it - LO-4's proportionality.
A stationary charge makes no magnetic field; only a current does. LO-4's premise stated negatively.
Widely separated lines mean a weak field - LO-6's 'interprets their spacing' in one line.
Repulsion as the sure test of magnetism is a property of permanent magnets; the frame has no permanent-magnetism outcome, so goal level. Frame gap.
Like poles repel - permanent-magnet pole interaction, which no outcome covers. Goal level rather than stretching LO-6, which is about field lines.
The stem pins the content: 'relationship between electricity and magnetism' is the magnetic effect of a current, LO-4 - unlike the Gilbert item, whose content has no outcome at all.
Shape of a straight conductor's field (concentric rings) - LO-4.
Direction of the field inside a bar magnet (south to north) - a bar-magnet field-line fact, LO-6. No current, so not LO-4.
Lodestone as the old name for magnetite is terminology from the history of the subject; no outcome covers it. Goal level. Frame gap.
Concentric circles in a plane perpendicular to the current - LO-4's straight-conductor pattern. Near-duplicate of item 34.
A neutron feels no magnetic force because it carries no charge - the charge condition on the LO-1 force.
Force is zero when the charge moves along B - the theta = 0 case of the LO-1 force.
Draw a uniform field as parallel, equidistant lines. Pure field-line drawing and spacing, LO-6.
Zero force on a stationary charged particle - the velocity condition on the LO-1 force; pairs with the charge-along-B item.
A current-carrying conductor in a field experiences a force - the bare statement of LO-1.
Asks for the name of the rule giving the direction of the force - Fleming's left-hand rule, named verbatim in LO-5.
50 Hz is a property of the domestic mains supply; LO-7 is the only outcome reaching domestic circuits. The frame has no A.C./D.C. outcome - recorded as a gap.
